nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of MoNiOₓ
nodes.procedure: 0.15 mmol (NH₄)₆Mo₇O₂₄·4H₂O and 4.5 mmol Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O were dissolved in 35 mL of deionized water and stirred thoroughly for 1 h. Then, a piece of nickel foam (NF) (2.5×3 cm²) and the configured solution were transferred to the autoclave sealed and maintained at 150°C for 15 h. At the end of the reaction and after the temperature was cooled down to room temperature, NF and precipitate inside the Teflon reactor were washed with ethanol and deionized water three times and dried at 60°C for 24 h. The grown Mo–Ni oxide nanoflakes were denoted as MoNiOₓ.
nodes.source_text: 2.1. Synthesis of MoNiOₓ ... The grown Mo–Ni oxide nanoflakes were denoted as MoNiOₓ.

nodes.name: NaBH₄ reduction and calcination of SF-MoNi₄/NiO
nodes.procedure: First of all, the prepared MoNiOₓ precursor was immersed in the NaBH₄ solution composed of 4 mg NaBH₄ and 20 mL deionized water for 30 min to obtain the SF-MoNiOₓ precursor. Secondly, it was calcined in a tube furnace, and heated to 400°C at a fixed ramp rate (5°C/min) under a flowing air atmosphere and held for 2 h, after being reduced to room temperature, the temperature was raised to 500°C under an Ar/H₂ atmosphere at a heating rate of 5°C/min and held for 1 h, and then it was naturally cooled to obtain SF-MoNi₄/NiO.

nodes.procedure: MoNi₄/NiO was synthesized the same way as SF-MoNi₄/NiO, except for the NaBH₄ solution treatment process. nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show uniformly distributed flower-like structures composed of ultrathin nanosheets that are much rougher and thinner for SF-MoNi4/NiO compared to MoNi4/NiO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images (Fig. 1b, c, e, and f) show uniformly distributed flower-like structures composed of ultrathin nanosheets of the SF-MoNi₄/NiO and MoNi₄/NiO and exhibiting the inherited nanosheet construction ... It is noteworthy that, compared with MoNi₄/NiO, SF-MoNi₄/NiO are much rougher (Fig. 1d and g), and it is thinner as can be seen from the atomic force microscope (AFM) (Fig. S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows SF-MoNi4/NiO closer to Ni0 than MoNi4/NiO; FT-EXAFS shows Ni–O at 1.47/1.50 Å and Ni–M at 2.05/2.03 Å; Ni–O coordination number declines from 3.3 (MoNi4/NiO) to 2.1 (SF-MoNi4/NiO).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XANES of the Ni K-edge in MoNi4/NiO was viewed to be between Ni foil and NiO... For SF-MoNi₄/NiO, the state of the Ni species is also between Ni0 and Ni2+ but is more closely aligned with Ni0... As shown in Fig. 3h, the FT-EXAFS spectra of the Ni K-edge show two notable peaks at 1.47 (1.50) and 2.05 (2.03) Å for SF-MoNi₄/NiO (and MoNi₄/NiO)... The fitting results reveal that the average CN of Ni–O bond declines from MoNi4/NiO (3.3) to SF-MoNi4/NiO (2.1).
